[P2] Revisit the equality conditions under rule 4. The new equality tests compare only parameterized `MapResult` types with null owners; their negative case changes only the item type. Removing either the raw-type comparison or the owner check leaves those assertions unchanged, so these added conditions lack the behavior-distinguishing tests required by “Every branch has a test that fails without it.” The claimed cache-key contract is therefore incompletely guarded. Please return to the design phase under rule 8, step 6, and establish which conditions the contract needs and how each will be demonstrated.

To suppress repeats, reply `/ai verdict deferred`, `/ai verdict false-positive`, or `/ai verdict out-of-scope` on the first nonblank line. Add rationale on later lines. A new `/ai verdict accepted` allows future repeats again.

The type parameter `U` does not appear in the argument, so `TypeToken<String> t = TypeToken.of(Integer.class)` compiles, and a `null` argument is accepted and fails later. Since `of` is new and unreleased, we can still think about the signature. Could this return `TypeToken<?>`, call `Objects.requireNonNull(type, ...)`, and keep the unchecked cast inside `MapOperation.mapResultType`? (Maybe also have a direct test of this case?)
